archetype.name: Rebuilding (fast and chaotic)
archetype.definition: A team coming off a 31-51 season that has started even worse, playing the league's fastest style while ranking 27th on both offense and defense, with its rotation still sorting out who belongs.

report.headline: The margin is real, but so are some fixable shooting numbers
report.take:
Chicago is 1-5, and nothing about the record is a fluke in either direction. Its W vs Pt Diff is 0 and the margin implies exactly one win. A Net Rtg of -14.9 ranks 29th. The Bulls are 27th in offensive rating and 27th in defensive rating, so there is no single leak to plug. The backdrop matters too: they slid from 39-43 to 31-51 last season with a -5.1 Net Rtg, and this start is a step further down, not a reset.

The identity is speed and volume. A Pace of 106.2 against a league average of 100.1 makes them the fastest team in the sheet. They take 47.9% of their shots from three (3rd), get to the line more than anyone (FT Rate 38.3%, 1st) and crash the offensive glass (ORB % 29.2, 9th). The plan creates plenty of possessions. It falls apart at the finish: they hit 28.1% from three, last in the league, so the eFG % of 48.2 is also last. The defense has the mirror-image problem. Opponents shoot 39.3% from three (28th) and take 35.5% of their shots at the rim (29th), so Chicago is both getting beaten into the paint and watching kick-outs fall.

The numbers hide how much of this is shooting variance and how much is personnel. A league-worst three-point percentage on that much volume should drift up, and opponents won't keep shooting 39.3% forever. That is real improvement waiting to happen. The lineup data, though, points at structural problems. Norman Powell is the one efficient scorer (61.7 TS %), and the team is +33.4 per 100 better with him on the floor. Jalen Smith is +23.3 on-off and is listed day-to-day. Meanwhile the wings grade D-, with Matas Buzelis at -16.2 and Leonard Miller at -32.5 on-off. Josh Giddey has 45 assists but a 46.5 TS %, and Tre Jones has been more productive in fewer minutes (BPM 3).

Where it heads: the last five games were a little less ugly than the season, at -10.4 a game, once the 92-135 opener at Toronto drops out. That is still a lottery team's margin. Expect the shooting to normalize enough to lift them from awful to merely bad. Expect the coming week, two games against a 6-1 Philadelphia defense and a trip to New York, to keep the record near the bottom of the Central.

strengths.title: Free throws and second chances
strengths.body: Chicago leads the league in FT Rate and sits top-ten in ORB %, so even a miss-heavy offense still creates extra points. This comes from attacking off the fast pace and sending bodies to the glass. That is effort and style, not luck, and it should hold. It is the reason the Bulls score a league-average-ish 113.5 a game despite shooting so poorly.

strengths.title: Powell is the engine that works
strengths.body: Norman Powell is scoring efficiently on meaningful usage, with a 61.7 TS % at 24.4 USG %. The team is far better with him on the floor than off it. He is the only high-minute player turning possessions into points at a good rate. An On-Off this extreme over six games will shrink, but the direction is clear.

strengths.title: Rim finishing defense holds up
strengths.body: Opponents get to the rim far too often, but they convert there at only 61.5%, 7th best in the league. Chicago's bigs are contesting the shots they get to. Smith's rebounding and positive on-off suggest he is a big part of that. If the perimeter containment improves, this is a foundation.

concerns.title: Three-point volume without makes
concerns.body: A top-three share of threes paired with the league's worst percentage is the costliest combination in basketball. It is why the eFG % is dead last. Some of it is variance: 28.1% is well below the league's 34.7%, and the team shot near 36% from deep last season, so it should climb. Even a normal shooting year leaves this offense below average, though.

concerns.title: Perimeter defense is leaking
concerns.body: Opponents are taking a huge share of shots at the rim and hitting 39.3% from three. Point guards have feasted, scoring 10.04 more than their own averages, the second-worst mark in the league. The opponents' three-point luck should cool. The dribble penetration is a containment problem, which shows up in the D-graded wings and D backcourt.

concerns.title: Wing minutes are bleeding points
concerns.body: Both listed wings carry deeply negative BPM and On-Off numbers, and the group grades D-. Leonard Miller's -32.5 On-Off is the worst among the rotation regulars. Unless the minutes shift toward the backcourt or the wings' shooting improves, this is a nightly hole.

trend.note: After last season's drop to 31-51, the Bulls opened 1-5 with a -15.83 per-game margin. The last five games were slightly better than the 92-135 opener, but still a -10.4 a game stretch.

weekAhead.headline: Two shots at Philadelphia's elite defense, plus a Knicks rematch
weekAhead.body:
Three games in a week: at Philadelphia, at New York, then Philadelphia at home. The 76ers are 6-1 with the league's second-best defensive rating at 105.4. They also take care of the ball better than anyone (TOV % 11.4, 1st), which starves Chicago of the run-outs its pace depends on. Their record runs a bit ahead of their play: a W vs Pt Diff of 2 is the league's highest. They are beatable on the glass, though, ranking last in ORB % and REB %. That gives the Bulls' offensive rebounding a real opening.

New York already beat Chicago 127-133 in Chicago. The Knicks are 2-4 and an inefficient shooting team (TS % 29th), so that game is the most winnable on paper. The problem is the Knicks own the league's best DRB %, which takes away Chicago's second-chance edge. Their wings grade F and give up 26.17 points a game to small forwards, a rare chance for Buzelis and Miller to produce. A 0-3 week is quite plausible. Stealing one would be a good result.

keyMatchups.title: Bulls' offensive glass vs Philadelphia
keyMatchups.body: Philadelphia is the league's worst offensive-rebounding team, with a below-average DRB %, while Chicago crashes hard. Against a defense this stingy in the half court, extra possessions may be the only way the Bulls keep up. If they don't win the rebounding margin, the games likely get away early.

keyMatchups.title: Chicago wings vs Knicks' weak wings
keyMatchups.body: New York's wings grade F and its defense has allowed big nights to small forwards. It is the softest spot on any defense Chicago sees this week. The Bulls' wings have struggled badly, so this game is a fair test of whether that is form or ability.

keyMatchups.title: Jalen Smith's availability
keyMatchups.body: Smith is day-to-day and carries one of the team's best on-off marks, plus the frontcourt's best rebounding. Without him, the rim defense and glass work that keep Chicago competitive both thin out.

weekAhead.watch: Whether Chicago's three-point percentage starts climbing off 28.1% against a Philadelphia defense that allows only 32.1% from deep. That is the clearest sign of whether the offense is unlucky or just bad.

restOfSeason.body:
With a W vs Pt Diff of 0, the record is an honest reflection of the margin, and that margin projects to only 14 wins over a full season. That pace is too pessimistic. Chicago's own three-point shooting is far below anything in its recent history, and opponents' 39.3% from deep is unlikely to hold, so both ends should drift toward normal. The free-throw rate, offensive rebounding and rim finishing look like real traits rather than noise.

What won't simply regress is the roster balance. The wing minutes are deeply negative, the backcourt grades D, and the team relies on Powell and Smith to be the positive on-court pieces. Expect a team in the low-to-mid 20s in wins with a Net Rtg somewhere around -6 to -9. That is better than now but worse than last year's 31-51, and firmly in the lottery.
swingFactors: How far the three-point shooting rebounds
Whether wing minutes stop bleeding points

confidence.note: Only six games, and shooting percentages are noisy this early, but the poor margin matches last season's decline.
